label: Market Explainer
headline: Gold, silver slide and the US AI sell-off: what it means for Indian markets
paras: Gold and silver fell again on Thursday, 19 November 2026. COMEX December gold settled 1.51% lower at $3,685.50 an ounce and December silver fell 1.55% to $44.36. On Friday morning MCX gold was down 3.94% at ₹1,22,435 per 10 grams and MCX silver down 6% at ₹1,48,034 per kg.

Why metals are falling: markets are pricing a December rate hike by the US Federal Reserve after hawkish Fed minutes, the dollar index has risen for eight straight sessions to 103.96, and the 10-year US Treasury yield is near 5.05%. The World Gold Council also points to selling by leveraged investors.

The AI sell-off: on Thursday the Nasdaq fell 2.25% to 23,879, the S&P 500 fell 2.02% to 7,176 and the Dow fell 2.19% to 49,097. Nvidia fell 3.30% despite strong quarterly results. On Friday Japan's Nikkei fell 4.28% and Korea's Kospi about 4.3%.

India: after a nine-month high on Thursday (Nifty 25,514.30, Sensex 83,021.75), the Nifty opened 0.57% lower at 25,368 and the Sensex 0.56% lower at 82,558.25 on Friday. IT stocks such as TCS and HCLTech gained in early trade, while Titan, JSW Steel and Tata Steel were among the top losers. FIIs bought ₹7,411 crore on 19 November, their eighth straight session of net buying.

scenes.title: Market Explainer
scenes.hook: Gold at a 14-month low. AI stocks sinking. What it means for India
scenes.voice: Gold just hit a fourteen month low, and Wall Street's AI trade is cracking. Here's what it means for Indian markets.

scenes.title: Gold and silver slide
scenes.voice: Gold and silver both fell about one and a half percent on Thursday. This morning, MCX gold is down almost four percent, and MCX silver six percent.

scenes.title: Why metals are falling

rows.label: Fed rate hike bets
rows.sub: Hawkish Fed minutes; December hike priced in

rows.label: Strong dollar
rows.sub: Dollar index up 8 sessions in a row

scenes.voice: The reason? Markets now expect the Fed to raise rates in December. A stronger dollar and US bond yields near five percent make gold, which pays no interest, less attractive.

scenes.title: US AI sell-off (Thursday)
scenes.voice: On Wall Street, the Nasdaq fell over two percent. Nvidia dropped more than three percent, even after strong results, as investors question how fast AI spending will pay off.

scenes.title: Asia this morning
scenes.voice: Asia took the hit this morning. Japan and Korea both fell more than four percent.

scenes.title: India: Friday open
scenes.voice: India is holding up far better. The Nifty opened only about half a percent lower, a day after hitting a nine month high.

scenes.title: Early movers (Nifty 50)
scenes.voice: Metal stocks slipped with global commodity prices, while IT and hospital stocks gained.

scenes.title: Why India is holding up

rows.label: Banks in focus
rows.sub: Foreign buying mainly in banking majors

rows.label: Cheaper metals
rows.sub: Drawing buying in autos and durables

scenes.voice: Foreign investors bought seven thousand four hundred crore rupees of Indian shares on Thursday, their eighth straight day of buying, mostly in banks. Cheaper metals have also drawn buying in auto stocks.
